This editor changes the live repository config object consumed by PNGPlaneAvatar.buildSinglePlaneAvatarModel, then rebuilds the avatar through the same path used by this preview. The game formula is assemblyY = (ratio - 0.5) × final model height, followed by the game’s separate final model height / 2 floor-root lift. Species parent inheritance, gender lookup, child scaling, and portraitScaleBySpecies remain active. The verification readout compares the requested ratio, the value stored by the repository model, its real assembly Y, final dimensions, and the game-style lift.
Leg bend (invisible hip/thigh/calf authoring)
Load an NPC to author a leg bend.
Each foot hangs off an invisible 2-bone leg running from the avatar's posterior anchor down to the foot (see docs/js/leg-bones.js) — the cyan/orange lines trace hip -> knee -> foot for the left/right leg. Unauthored, the knee just marks the straight-line midpoint and the leg tracks the foot automatically through the gait. "Edit leg bend" attaches a rotate-only gizmo to the left thigh; the right leg mirrors it sideways automatically. The edit applies to the currently loaded NPC's species+gender and is written into this session's live config — use the copy/download buttons to get the exact proceduralFeet.legBend block to paste into scratchbones-config.js.
Per-species imported foot models (.glb)
No imported foot GLBs for this species.
Import a GLB to inspect and replace its materials.
Open this directly with the always-visible Foot Models button beside Placement. GLBs are kept for this browser session and replace the procedural foot on their assigned side. Imported models preserve their proportions, are normalized to the procedural foot height and then enlarged to 200%, centered in X/Z, and seated on the same jump-safe local contact baseline. Each detected GLB material now uses the furniture author’s surface-PNG workflow: choose a repository/custom PNG, optionally adaptive-shade-fill it with body color, Kenkari black, Tletingan bone white, or a custom color, then choose original/generated UVs, stretch, or tile mapping, quarter-turn rotation, and PNG transparency. GLBs without UVs automatically receive box-projected UVs, and PNG overrides normalize glossy or metallic source materials to a matte foot surface. A “Both feet” import is cloned without mirroring; use separate left/right files when the models are asymmetric.
Normal + sprint transformsBlending
neutral 1.00 · forward 0.00 · backward 0.00 · left 0.00 · right 0.00
The four normal transforms are 100% movement endpoints relative to the character’s own facing. Sprint Forward is one separate authored sprint endpoint. At runtime that one sprint pose is spatially rotated around the character’s local vertical axis to follow backward, sideways, and diagonal travel, so you do not need four sprint keyframes. Select any endpoint to preview it without rotating the locomotion root, then edit it with the 3D gizmo or exact fields. Normal runtime weights come from actual velocity projected into character-local axes—not the camera or world. In Drunken movement, stopping blends toward the opposite normal endpoint by Recoil distance at Recoil speed, then returns at Rebalance speed. Idle motion slowly shifts toward low-intensity random combinations of the four normal transforms.
{}
Imported from docs/game.js. Regular uses the game’s 238 px/s target speed, 980 acceleration, 1320 sharp-turn acceleration, 1850 stopping force, 0.18 cardinal bias, and joystick response (56 px radius, 0.14 deadzone, 0.82 response curve), scaled to this 3D preview. Drunken motion modifies that same pipeline rather than replacing its controls. Its four default endpoint transforms are loaded from the supplied movement settings; stop recoil uses their character-relative opposites, and idle rocking blends slowly toward seeded random character-relative directions. Sprinting uses one editable Sprint Forward transform, rotated around the character’s local vertical axis for every travel direction.

Equipped position on avatar

This is the parent transform that places the completed two-plane tool relative to the avatar. X is side-to-side, Y is height, and Z is forward/back. “Snap to hand” uses the avatar plane renderer’s measured hand attachment metadata as a starting point.

Front PNG plane

The front sprite begins at 0° pitch. Its base geometry preserves the PNG’s native 320×663 aspect ratio.

Top PNG plane

The top sprite begins at exactly 90° pitch relative to an ordinary PNG plane. Its base geometry preserves the PNG’s native 318×247 aspect ratio.

Projected center of mass: waiting for planted feet.
Authoring physics uses a separate vertical capsule fitted to the PNG plane's overall width and height, then extruded only slightly through Z. Physics plane thickness controls that shallow depth, and a bright cyan outline plus translucent fill remain visible at rest and in motion. It is bake metadata only and never replaces or modifies the game's combat hitbox. All body pose and ragdoll rotation now uses the repository's existing posterior/hip anchor as its origin; that exact source and local pivot are retained in new exports. Knockdowns and deaths keep rotating after first contact until the capsule settles onto its nearest broad face; Flat-collapse strength controls that fall and Flat-collapse damping removes energy once flat. Hit reactions still project the moving torso center of mass onto a support capsule formed by the planted feet. When that projection leaves support, ground reaction pulls toward the nearest support point, the torso leans there immediately, and a bounded alternating recovery step widens the stance if needed. Y rotation remains free throughout the authored impact. Drunken directional and sprint poses contribute rotation and scale but no pose-space body translation; gameplay movement remains the only displacement owner. The bake stores the solved hip plus thigh/calf rotations, fixed bone lengths, real foot-assembly transform, and sampled ground level. Preview uses forward kinematics from those recorded bones, so diagonal blending cannot shorten the legs and no foot is ever treated as a locked ground target. At low Footing, locomotion emphasizes irregular foot reach, crossing placements, toe angle, and occasional wide corrective steps instead of relying on torso sway alone. Maximum clip duration is only a safety cap: live physics ends after 0.16 seconds of confirmed visual stillness, and imported or preset micro-drift is perceptually trimmed before playback. If Preview automatic return is enabled, playback adds a preview-only bridge from the raw final key into the current gameplay pose after recording stops; with blend auto-walk enabled, that destination is the live Footing-based walking gait rather than idle. The bridge never enters frames, events, duration, or blend-space exports. With Gameplay owns horizontal X/Z knockback enabled, exported clips still retain vertical Y body movement while gameplay supplies only horizontal displacement. The Impact and Footing-break spin throw banks are pre-loaded from this repository's real exported clip data; Full Stun has no separate authored clip and instead holds the settled final frame of whichever direction of Footing-break spin throw just played, and Recovery Somersault is intentionally left for the live game to generate elsewhere.
